title: Lint coverage gap: e2e/ is outside every package's lint script, so turbo lint green ≠ repo lint clean
body:
Found during #4045 (PR #4450): repo-root `pnpm exec eslint .` reports **3 errors under `e2e/`** (2× `no-useless-assignment`, 1× `preserve-caught-error`) that `turbo run lint` never sees, because no package's lint script covers `e2e/`. `main` has this today; turbo stays green.

## Why this is a card and not noise

The repo's load-bearing lint check is `turbo run lint` (that is what CI runs). Any directory outside every package's lint script is a surface where lint errors accrete invisibly — the same shape as the coverage-gate blind spots #4347 just closed for tsc chains: a green gate over a population that silently excludes part of the repo. Today it is 3 stylistic errors; the gap, not the 3 errors, is the defect.

## Options for whoever takes it

1. Add a root-level lint script (or a dedicated `e2e` lint task in turbo) that covers `e2e/`, fix the 3 errors it surfaces.
2. If `e2e/` is deliberately unlinted, encode that decision: add it to a documented ignore so root `eslint .` and turbo agree, and the next person doesn't rediscover the discrepancy.

Either way the invariant to land is: **root `eslint .` and `turbo run lint` agree on what is clean** — one resolver, one answer.

Filed unassigned as an observation; measurement details in PR #4450's report/body.
